text:
emma: Heads-up — after the SDK retry tweak last night the sample-app in prod started delivering duplicate webhooks to a few customers. Not a total outage but ~0.8% of deliveries are duplicated. Anyone else seeing this?
ci-bot: deploy: go-sdk@v1.12.0 rolled out to prod (2026-03-23T02:58:12Z) :rocket:
raj: On it. Do we have request/response logs showing the 429 -> retry path? Crucial detail: is the server sending Retry-After and are our SDKs honoring it?
emma: Pasting sanitized consumer logs (timestamps trimmed):
```
[webhook] POST /deliver -> 429
Response headers: Retry-After: 3

[webhook] client retry #1 after 0.1s -> 200 (duplicate payload delivered)
[webhook] client retry #2 after 0.2s -> 200
```
mike: Quick observation: Node SDK has code to parse Retry-After both as delta-seconds and HTTP-date. Go SDK's earlier change used strconv.Atoi(Retry-After) only, so it crashes/parses wrongly when servers return a date string. If the header is mis-parsed we fall back to immediate retry which can cause duplicates.
alyssa: Also, sample-app callbacks don't include an idempotency header on outgoing webhooks — they assumed receiver would dedupe. That's fragile when retries are aggressive.
raj: Actionable plan suggestion: 1) Ensure all official SDKs honor Retry-After header (support both integer and HTTP-date formats). 2) Add a safe-replay opt-in: SDK should attach an X-Idempotency-Key UUID by default for outgoing webhooks (or provide a helper) and document the contract. 3) Emit a metric when we detect duplicate deliveries so product can monitor regressions.
mike: Example Node handling that works (we already have similar):
```js
const ra = res.headers['retry-after'];
let wait = 0;
if (/^\d+$/.test(ra)) wait = parseInt(ra, 10);
else wait = Math.max(0, new Date(ra) - Date.now()) / 1000;
await sleep(wait + jitter());
```
raj: For Go I'd suggest this approach (pseudo): parse as int, if fail try http.ParseTime then subtract time.Now(); clamp to >=0. Also cap max backoff.
emma: On the idempotency side I propose default header name X-Redwood-Idempotency and a small helper that returns uuidv4 if none provided. sample-apps should opt-in or set policy in quickstart.
alyssa: Could we add an onboarding lint/test that fails CI if a sample-app sends webhooks without an idempotency header? That would catch this class of bug earlier.
mike: I'll open two PRs: go-sdk fix (parse Retry-After + unit tests for delta-seconds and RFC1123/HTTP-date) and sample-apps change (attach idempotency header, add e2e harness). Linking to the test harness: repo://samples/webhook-replay-test (internal).
raj: Acceptance criteria for the PRs: parsing tests for both header formats, integration test where server returns HTTP-date -> client waits accordingly, and a telemetry event for duplicate_webhook_detected (count + sample keys).
emma: For rollback safety, can we also add a config toggle that reverts to legacy behavior? I don't want another surprise while we ship.
raj: Good call. Add a feature flag "honor_retry_after" default true, and a runtime config for idempotency header generation.
alyssa: I'll add the CI lint rule and a small doc snippet in the devex onboarding guide about webhook best practices.
mike: Opening PRs now, will tag @raj @emma for review, and add the tests. ETA today EOD.
emma: Awesome, thanks. Please also add a short note to the release notes and a migration checklist for customers using self-hosted SDKs.
raj: Noted. I'll also add a quick smoke test to our staging fleet that simulates a 429 with both numeric and HTTP-date Retry-After values.
emma: Thanks all :thumbsup: Action items: mike -> PRs + tests, raj -> staging smoke, alyssa -> CI lint + docs, emma -> release notes.
